<h5 align="left" style="font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></h5>


<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>FOREIGN CURRENCY EXCHANGE RISK </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">We transact business in various foreign countries and are, therefore, subject to risk of foreign currency exchange rate fluctuations. Although
Flex uses financial instruments to hedge certain foreign currency risks, we are not fully protected against foreign currency fluctuations and our reported results of operations could be affected by changes in foreign currency exchange rates. To
manage our exposures and mitigate the impact of currency fluctuations on the operations of our foreign subsidiaries, we hedge our main transactional exposures through the use of foreign exchange forward and option contracts. Accordingly, the
combined statement of operations include the impact of Flex&#8217;s derivative financial instruments that are deemed to be associated with our operations and has been allocated to us utilizing a reasonable allocation method. The recorded fair values
of the associated assets and liabilities were not material to the Company&#8217;s combined financial position. Following the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off,</FONT> we intend to implement a standalone foreign currency risk management
program. </P>

directorships resulting from an increase in the number of directors will be distributed among the three classes so that, as nearly as possible, each class will consist of one-third of the directors. The division of our board of directors into three
classes with staggered three-year terms may delay or prevent a change of our management or a change of control. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">The Spinco Board of
Directors is expected to adopt corporate governance guidelines (the &#8220;Corporate Governance Guidelines&#8221;) that will provide a framework for the effective governance of Spinco. The Corporate Governance Guidelines will address significant
corporate governance issues, including, among other things: the appointment, role, and responsibilities of Spinco&#8217;s Lead Independent Director, if any; director nominee qualifications; director independence; limitations on director service on
other boards; director orientation and continuing education; annual performance evaluations of the Spinco Board of Directors and committees; and succession planning and management development. A copy of the Corporate Governance Guidelines will be
available at our website at axiomsolutions.com. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:24pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center"><B>Director Independence </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">The Spinco Board of Directors will annually review the relationship that each director has with Spinco. Following such annual review, only
those directors who the Spinco Board of Directors affirmatively determines do not have a relationship which, in the opinion of the Spinco Board of Directors, would interfere with the exercise of independent judgment in carrying out the
responsibilities of a director, under the listing standards of Nasdaq, will be considered independent directors. At the time of the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off,</FONT> the Corporate Governance Guidelines are expected to adopt the
definition of independence described in the director independence requirements for Nasdaq-listed companies. In doing so, the Spinco Board of Directors will take into account certain factors listed in the Corporate Governance Guidelines and such
other factors as it may deem relevant. A majority of the Spinco Board of Directors will be comprised of independent directors upon completion of the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off.</FONT> We expect that all directors, except Ms. Advaithi
who will be the Chief Executive Officer of Spinco, will meet the independence requirements set forth in the listing standards of Nasdaq at the time of the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off.</FONT> There are no family relationships among any
of our directors or executive officers. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:24pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center"><B>Board Committees </B></P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">The Spinco Board of Directors will not have a policy with respect to whether the roles of Chair of the Spinco Board of Directors (&#8220;Chair

employee. We believe the leadership structure of the Spinco Board of Directors at any point in time should be based upon an assessment of the needs of the Spinco Board of Directors and the Company at the time after giving consideration to, among
other things, Spinco&#8217;s business plans, strategic opportunities, and succession planning priorities. The Spinco Board of Directors will also consider the views of shareholders, including as it relates to director independence, as well as
corporate governance and industry trends. Spinco&#8217;s Corporate Governance Guidelines will provide that the Spinco Board of Directors will appoint a Lead Independent Director if the Chair of the Board is not an independent director under Nasdaq
listing standards or if the Spinco Board of Directors otherwise deems it appropriate. Spinco&#8217;s Lead Independent Director, if appointed, will play an important role in maintaining effective independent oversight of the Company. </P>

the class and number of shares of our common stock beneficially owned by the shareholder as of the date the shareholder gives written notice; a description of all arrangements or understandings between the shareholder and the director candidate and

experience for at least the previous five years; the principal occupation or employment of the director candidate; the class and number of shares of our common stock beneficially owned by the director candidate; the consent of the director candidate
to serve as a member of the Spinco Board of Directors if appointed or elected; and any other information required to be disclosed with respect to a director nominee in solicitations for proxies for the election of directors pursuant to applicable
rules of the SEC. The committee may require additional information as it deems reasonably required to determine the eligibility of the director candidate to serve as a member of the Spinco Board of Directors. Shareholders recommending candidates for
consideration by our board in connection with the next annual meeting of shareholders should submit their written recommendation no later than &#8195;&#8195;&#8195;&#8195; of the year of that meeting. The committee will evaluate director candidates
recommended by shareholders for election to the Spinco Board of Directors in the same manner and using the same criteria as it uses for any other director candidate. If the committee determines that a shareholder-recommended candidate is suitable
for membership on the Spinco Board of Directors, it will include the candidate in the pool of candidates to be considered for nomination upon the occurrence of the next vacancy on the Spinco Board of Directors or in connection with the next annual

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center"><B><A NAME="rom42824_14"></A>COMPENSATION DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Introduction </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">During Spinco&#8217;s
fiscal year ended March&nbsp;31, 2026, Spinco was not yet incorporated, was not an independent company and did not have a compensation committee or any other committee serving a similar function. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">For purposes of this Compensation Discussion and Analysis (&#8220;CD&amp;A&#8221;) and the disclosure that follows, Ms.&nbsp;Advaithi, who
currently serves as the Chief Executive Officer of Flex and is expected to serve as our Chief Executive Officer; Mr.&nbsp;Krumm, who currently serves as the Chief Financial Officer of Flex and is expected to serve our Chief Financial Officer;
Mr.&nbsp;Tan, who currently serves as the Chief Operating Officer of Flex and is expected to serve as our Chief Operating Officer; and Mr.&nbsp;Offer, who currently serves as Executive Vice President and General Counsel of Flex and is expected to
serve as Executive Vice President and General Counsel of Spinco are the only individuals who served as executive officers of Flex during fiscal year 2026 and are expected to serve in an executive officer role at Spinco. We refer to these individuals
as our &#8220;named executive officers&#8221; or &#8220;NEOs&#8221; for purposes of the CD&amp;A and the disclosure that follows. The CD&amp;A discusses Flex&#8217;s historical compensation programs as applied to Ms.&nbsp;Advaithi and Messrs. Krumm,
Tan and Offer, and outlines certain aspects of Spinco&#8217;s anticipated post-Distribution compensation structure for those individuals. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">At the time of the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off,</FONT> Spinco will have in place executive compensation programs, policies, and
practices for its executive officers that are generally similar to those of Flex. Spinco is currently a part of Flex, and its Compensation and People Committee will be formed in connection with
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">the&nbsp;Spin-Off.&nbsp;We</FONT> expect the executive compensation programs, policies and practices for our executive officers will align incentives more closely with Spinco&#8217;s performance, strategic
initiatives, industry peers and the long-term interests of our shareholders, which is expected to help us attract, retain and motivate highly qualified personnel. Accordingly, after the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off,</FONT> we will
review the compensation for all of our executive officers and determine the appropriate compensation, benefits and perquisites for them, and accordingly the compensation, benefits and perquisites provided to them after the <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off</FONT> will not necessarily be the same as those discussed below. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Executive Summary </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify"><B><I>Flex Practice </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">Flex&#8217;s pay programs align executive compensation with Flex&#8217;s performance and shareholder value creation. Flex uses a mix of
performance metrics that reward different aspects of company achievement across short-term and long-term objectives. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify"><B><I>Going Forward
</I></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">After the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off,</FONT> we will review the compensation for all of our executive officers and
determine the appropriate compensation, benefits and perquisites for them, and accordingly the compensation, benefits and perquisites provided to them after the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off</FONT> will not necessarily be the same as
those discussed below. </P>

<TD VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="justify" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt">To place a greater emphasis on driving performance and delivering Flex shareholder value</P></TD></TR>

<TD VALIGN="bottom">&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="justify" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt">Increased the maximum payout potential to 250% of target (from 200%); capped at 200% of target when relative TSR is in the
bottom quartile of the peer group</P></TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom">&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="justify" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt">To incentivize exceptional EPS performance over a three-year period, while ensuring payouts are supported by adequate Flex

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">Flex&#8217;s executive compensation program is structured to be competitive and allow Flex to attract and retain a high-caliber leadership
team. Further, it is intended to provide direct alignment between pay and performance. The illustrations below show the key elements of Flex&#8217;s direct compensation for its NEOs in fiscal year 2026 and how those elements were allocated. A
majority of target pay is performance-based, with 92% <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">at-risk</FONT> for our CEO and 83% <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">at-risk</FONT> for Flex&#8217;s other NEOs (on average), as detailed below. </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">We anticipate that our executive compensation program upon the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off</FONT> will generally include the same

its decision-making with respect to the Spinco&#8217;s executive compensation program and ensure that such program supports Spinco&#8217;s recruitment and retention needs and is fair and efficient. Consistent with the determination of the Flex peer
group, the Flex Compensation and People Committee selected companies for inclusion in Spinco&#8217;s peer group based on (1) comparability of revenues and market capitalization (2) the extent to which they compete with Spinco for executive talent
because they operate in a similar industry, and (3) other qualitative factors such as business fit and complexity. This compensation peer group is comprised of the following companies: </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Compensation Philosophy </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify"><B><I>Flex Practice </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">Flex&#8217;s compensation philosophy centers on meaningful
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">pay-for-performance</FONT></FONT> alignment. Flex&#8217;s compensation programs link executive pay to Flex&#8217;s short-term and long-term objectives and the creation of shareholder
value. Flex designs its compensation programs to attract, retain, and motivate top executive talent by offering competitive pay opportunities tied to rigorous performance goals, while balancing the need to avoid excessive risk-taking and maintaining
cost discipline. Flex actively manages its <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">pay-for-performance</FONT></FONT> philosophy as described below. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1.150000em; font-family:Times New Roman">Flex&#8217;s base salaries and target cash compensation are competitively positioned for our NEOs to manage fixed costs and emphasize paying for

<TD VALIGN="bottom">&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom"><DIV STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt; display: table-row;" ALIGN="justify"><DIV STYLE="display: table-cell">
<P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.500000em; font-family:Times New Roman">&#149;</P></DIV><DIV STYLE="display: table-cell">
<P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1.150000em; font-family:Times New Roman">Programs are designed to link pay delivery to the achievement of <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">pre-determined</FONT> performance goals that
directly correlate with enhanced shareholder value.</P></DIV></DIV>
<P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P><DIV STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt; display: table-row;" ALIGN="justify"><DIV STYLE="display: table-cell">

<P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1.150000em; font-family:Times New Roman">92% of Ms.&nbsp;Advaithi&#8217;s fiscal year 2026 target total direct compensation was <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">at-risk</FONT> (excluding the
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">one-time</FONT> supplemental performance-based equity award granted in fiscal 2026) and, on average, 83% of target total direct compensation for its other NEOs was

based on stock price and/or relative TSR performance. Incentive outcomes are based on a formulaic calculation of results against <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">pre-determined</FONT> financial or <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">TSR-based</FONT>
performance targets.</P></DIV></DIV> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P><DIV STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt; display: table-row;" ALIGN="justify"><DIV STYLE="display: table-cell">

<P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1.150000em; font-family:Times New Roman">Formulaic funding results under the annual incentive plan are modified based on individual performance <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">(+/-10</FONT>
percentage points).</P></DIV></DIV> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P><DIV STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt; display: table-row;" ALIGN="justify"><DIV STYLE="display: table-cell">

<P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1.150000em; font-family:Times New Roman">The Flex Board of Directors, or the Flex Compensation and People Committee if so delegated by the Flex Board of Directors, maintains the authority to
adjust annual incentive bonus payouts if such payouts do not align with Flex&#8217;s overall performance.</P></DIV></DIV></TD></TR>

<P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1.150000em; font-family:Times New Roman">While measurement of short-term results maintains <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">day-to-day</FONT></FONT> focus,
Flex believes that shareholder value is built over the long term.</P></DIV></DIV>
<P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P><DIV STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt; display: table-row;" ALIGN="justify"><DIV STYLE="display: table-cell">

<P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1.150000em; font-family:Times New Roman">For Ms.&nbsp;Advaithi&#8217;s fiscal year 2026 target total direct compensation, 78% was in the form of long-term incentives, <FONT

granted in fiscal 2026). On average, 64% of target total direct compensation for our other NEOs was in the form of long-term incentives, tied to achievement of the same objectives as Ms.&nbsp;Advaithi. For additional information on
Ms.&nbsp;Advaithi&#8217;s <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">one-time</FONT> supplemental performance-based equity award, see the section titled &#8220;<I>Other Long-Term Incentive Compensation Award Granted during FY26</I>&#8221; on page

guidelines.</P></DIV></DIV></TD></TR>

<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Compensation-Setting Process and Decisions </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify"><B><I>Flex Practice </I></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Alignment with
Compensation and Corporate Governance Best Practices </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">The Flex Compensation and People Committee regularly reviews Flex&#8217;s
compensation programs, peer company data, and best practices in executive compensation. Flex has adopted corporate governance and compensation practices and policies that the Flex Compensation and People Committee, along with the Flex Board of
Directors, believes help to advance its compensation goals and philosophy. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE CELLSPACING="0" CELLPADDING="0" WIDTH="100%" BORDER="0" STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt" ALIGN="center">


<TR>

<TD WIDTH="50%"></TD>

<TD VALIGN="bottom" WIDTH="1%"></TD>
<TD WIDTH="48%"></TD></TR>
<TR STYLE="page-break-inside:avoid ; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:8pt">
<TD VALIGN="bottom" STYLE="border-bottom:1.00pt solid #000000"> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>What Flex Does</B></P></TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom" STYLE="border-bottom:1.00pt solid #000000"> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>What Flex Does Not Do</B></P></TD></TR>


<TR STYLE="page-break-inside:avoid ; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt">
<TD VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">The Flex Compensation and People Committee is composed entirely of independent members with a robust review process.</P>
<P STYLE="font-size:6pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt" align="left">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Flex uses a
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">pay-for-performance</FONT></FONT> executive compensation model that focuses primarily on corporate performance, with the majority of executive compensation <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">at-risk</FONT> and long-term.</P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">Flex
maintains a recoupment policy so Flex can clawback compensation paid to an executive officer in the event of a material restatement of financial results.</P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt" align="left">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">The Flex Compensation and People Committee retains an independent compensation advisor.</P>
<P STYLE="font-size:6pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt" align="left">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">Flex conducts regular shareholder outreach and considers
shareholder advisory votes and views in determining executive compensation strategies.</P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt" align="left">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">Flex maintains robust share ownership guidelines for NEOs and directors.</P></TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom"> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">Flex does not enter into NEO employment agreements.</P>
<P STYLE="font-size:6pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt" align="left">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">Flex does not pay severance in the event of an
executive&#8217;s voluntary resignation or retirement.</P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt" align="left">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">Flex does not allow hedging or short sales of Company equity, and Flex does not permit using our shares as collateral for margin accounts or
pledging of Company equity as collateral for loans.</P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt" align="left">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">Flex does not provide excise tax <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">gross-ups</FONT> with respect to compensation provided in connection with a
change of control event.</P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt" align="left">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">Flex does not have automatic
single-trigger accelerated vesting of equity awards upon a change of control.</P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt" align="left">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">Flex does not provide excessive or <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-customary</FONT> executive perquisites.</P>
<P STYLE="font-size:6pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt" align="left">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">Flex does not pay dividends or dividend equivalents on our
unvested equity awards.</P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt" align="left">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">Flex does not permit option/SAR
repricing (including cash buyouts) under our equity incentive plan without shareholder approval.</P></TD></TR>
</TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Flex Compensation and People Committee </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">The Flex Compensation and People Committee oversees compensation of its CEO, all other NEOs, and other executive officers, recommending
appropriate pay levels to the Flex Board of Directors. The Committee also administers Flex&#8217;s equity compensation plans, evaluates the effectiveness of its executive compensation programs, monitors <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">say-on-pay</FONT></FONT> results, and reviews talent assessment and succession planning. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">The Flex Compensation
and People Committee regularly assesses Flex&#8217;s compensation programs to ensure they support Flex&#8217;s business and human capital strategies. It also monitors market trends and changes in competitive pay practices. Based on these reviews,
the Committee may approve program changes or recommend such changes to the Flex Board of Directors. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Flex Independent Consultants and Advisors </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">The Flex Compensation and People Committee has the authority to retain and terminate any independent,
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">third-party</FONT> compensation consultants and to obtain advice and assistance from internal and external legal, </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center">152 </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">
accounting, and other advisors. During fiscal year 2026, the Flex Compensation and People Committee retained FW Cook as its independent compensation consultant. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">FW Cook furnished the Flex Compensation and People Committee reports on the following topics: Flex peer group composition, compensation data
and analysis relating to the compensation of Flex&#8217;s executive officers, short- and long-term compensation program design, compensation program risk assessment, annual share utilization and shareholder dilution levels resulting from equity
plans, executive share ownership and retention values, perquisites reviews, and regulatory updates. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">The Flex Compensation and People
Committee confirmed that there are no personal or business relationships between any FW Cook employee and any member of the Flex Compensation and People Committee or any of its executive officers beyond the Flex relationship. Based on this
information and other factors, including the factors set forth under Rule <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">10C-1</FONT> under the Exchange Act, the Flex Compensation and People Committee assessed the independence of FW Cook and concluded that no
conflict of interest exists that would prevent FW Cook from independently advising the Flex Compensation and People Committee. Outside of engaging on executive and director compensation and related matters, FW Cook does not provide any other
services to Flex. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Role of Executive Officers in Flex&#8217;s Compensation Decisions </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">The Flex Compensation and People Committee meets with Flex&#8217;s CEO and other executives to obtain recommendations with respect to the
structure of Flex&#8217;s compensation programs. The CEO and certain other executives also assess the performance of other individual executives and make recommendations regarding their compensation. Decisions related to the compensation of the CEO
(including recommendations to the Flex Board of Directors regarding the same) are made independently by the Flex Compensation and People Committee, without input from management. In addition, Flex&#8217;s CEO and other executives develop
recommendations for performance measures and target performance goals under Flex&#8217;s incentive plans based on Flex management&#8217;s business forecast&#8212;both at Flex and segment levels. These recommendations are approved by the Flex
Compensation and People Committee as well as by the Flex Board of Directors when appropriate. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Going Forward </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">The Spinco Compensation and People Committee will determine its appropriate role and the appropriate role of Spinco management, and independent
members of the Spinco Board of Directors in designing and approving executive officer compensation. Initially, the roles of each party are expected to be similar to Flex&#8217;s process. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">After <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">the&nbsp;Spin-Off,&nbsp;the</FONT> Spinco Compensation and People Committee will retain an independent
compensation consultant to advise on executive and director compensation matters. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Flex Executive Compensation Peer Group </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">Relying upon data provided by Flex&#8217;s independent compensation consultant, the Flex Compensation and People Committee undertakes a review,
on an annual basis, of the compensation peers that Flex uses to provide insight into market-competitive executive pay programs, levels and practices. The criteria used to develop the peer group were largely unchanged from fiscal year 2025,
continuing with revenue and market cap as the financial measures, as well as similar industry focus and publicly listed companies with headquarters in the U.S. as the other selection criteria. Applying these criteria, carried over from fiscal year
2025, did not result in any peer group changes &#8211; Flex continued with the same 14 peer companies as in fiscal year 2025. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify"><B><I>Going Forward </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">We anticipate that our executive compensation process upon the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off</FONT> will generally follow the same
process as Flex&#8217;s executive compensation process. Following the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off,</FONT> our Compensation and People Committee will review all aspects of its process and may make adjustments that it believes are
appropriate in establishing our executive compensation process. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">Further, the Flex Compensation and People Committee, with recommendations
from Semler Brossy, adopted a peer group for Spinco to help inform its decision-making with respect to the Spinco&#8217;s executive compensation program and ensure that such program supports the Company&#8217;s recruitment and retention needs and is
fair and efficient. Consistent with the determination of the Flex peer group, the Flex Compensation and People Committee selected companies for inclusion in Spinco&#8217;s peer group based on (1) comparability of revenues and market capitalization
(2) the extent to which they compete with the Company for executive talent because they operate in a similar industry, and (3) other qualitative factors such as business fit and complexity. This compensation peer group is comprised of the following
companies: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

growth. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">Adjusted OP acts as both a metric within the plan, and the overall funding metric of Flex&#8217;s global bonus program, as
illustrated below on page 158. Adjusted OP achievement generates an enterprise-wide funding pool based on the same adjusted OP targets as used for the Corporate NEO bonus plan, which acts to ensure affordability and alignment to shareholder returns.
Flex uses a range around OP, where aggregate bonus payouts must be within <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">+/-20%</FONT> of Corporate adjusted OP achievement. This maintains the connection between enterprise-wide bonus plan results and payouts as
well as pay for performance alignment. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">Flex continued with an individual performance modifier to the incentive bonus plan for fiscal year
2026, which can adjust the final bonus payout +/- 10 percentage points. Final bonus payouts are subject to the bonus plan cap of 200% of target. </P>

</TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Non-GAAP</FONT> Adjustments </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">Flex used adjusted <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</FONT> performance measures (adjusted OP and adjusted FCF) for its incentive bonus
plan in fiscal year 2026, and adjusted EPS in its fiscal 2026 adjusted EPS growth PSU grants. Using adjusted measures eliminates the distorting effect of certain unusual income or expense items. The adjusted performance measures are consistent with
those used in Flex&#8217;s quarterly earnings releases. The adjustments are intended to align award payout opportunities with the underlying growth of Flex&#8217;s business and avoid misalignment in outcomes based on unusual items. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">In calculating <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</FONT> financial measures, Flex excluded certain items to make it easier to compare
Flex&#8217;s operating performance on a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">period-to-period</FONT></FONT> basis because such items are not, in the Flex Compensation and People Committee&#8217;s view, related to
Flex&#8217;s ongoing operational performance. The <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</FONT> measures are used to more accurately evaluate Flex&#8217;s operating performance, to calculate return on investment, and to benchmark performance
against competitors. For fiscal year 2026, <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</FONT> adjustments consisted of excluding intangible amortization, customer-related asset impairments (recoveries); restructuring charges; <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">after-tax</FONT> stock-based compensation expense; <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">one-time</FONT> legal impacts; investment impairments; equity in earnings; and other tax impacts. All adjustments are subject to approval
by the Flex Compensation and People Committee to ensure that payout levels are consistent with performance. See Annex A to this information statement for a reconciliation of GAAP to <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</FONT> financial
measures. For purposes of calculating performance under Flex&#8217;s incentive bonus plan in fiscal year 2026, Flex has excluded the impact from extraordinary items or events that would have had an unanticipated impact, corporate transactions
(including acquisitions or dispositions), and other unusual or nonrecurring items. </P>

<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify"><B><I>Going Forward </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">Following the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off,</FONT> we anticipate that our Compensation and People Committee will develop an
incentive bonus plan focused on near-term operational and financial goals that support our business objectives, while also allowing for meaningful pay differentiation tied to performance of individuals and groups. We have not yet identified the
specific performance measures that will apply under the Spinco plan following the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off.</FONT> Our new incentive bonus plan will be prorated for our partial fiscal year starting on April 1, 2027. The first full
year of our incentive bonus plan will be from January 1, 2028 through December 31, 2028. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Long-Term Share-Based Incentive Compensation </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify"><B><I>Flex Practice </I></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">In
June 2025, the Flex Board of Directors, upon the recommendation of the Flex Compensation and People Committee, granted share-based long-term incentives to Flex&#8217;s senior executives as an incentive to maximize Flex&#8217;s long-term performance
and drive shareholder value creation. These awards are designed to align the interests of NEOs with those of Flex&#8217;s shareholders and to give each NEO a significant incentive to manage Flex from the perspective of an owner with a direct stake
in the business. Long-term equity awards are also intended to promote retention, since unvested shares are forfeited if an executive voluntarily leaves Flex. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">One-third</FONT> of the long-term incentive value was delivered in the form of service-based RSUs. rTSR PSUs
represent 20% of Flex&#8217;s executive officers&#8217; share-based long-term incentive awards (based on face value of the awards) in fiscal year 2026 and the remaining 47% was delivered in the form of adjusted EPS growth PSUs. The actual grant
value mix disclosed in the tables of this information statement may deviate from this 33/20/47 RSU/rTSR PSU/EPS PSU mix due to the Monte Carlo accounting valuation required by SEC rules to be used for the tabular disclosure of rTSR PSUs. The Flex
Compensation and People Committee believes this targeted <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">one-third/two-thirds</FONT></FONT> allocation between RSUs and PSUs links long-term compensation to Flex&#8217;s long-term
performance and shareholder outcomes and promotes retention. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">In addition to the awards granted in June 2025 under Flex&#8217;s fiscal
year 2026 long-term incentive compensation program, the Flex Board of Directors, upon the recommendation of the Flex Compensation and People Committee, granted a one-time performance-based long-term incentive equity award to our CEO for the
achievement of rigorous performance goals related to Flex&#8217;s CPI business. See below section titled &#8220;Other Long-Term Incentive Compensation Award Granted During FY26&#8221; on page&nbsp;164. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Restricted Share Unit Awards (RSUs) </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify"><FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">One-third</FONT> of each NEO&#8217;s fiscal year 2026 share-based long-term incentive award is in the form of RSUs. These service-based RSUs vest in three equal installments on the first three anniversaries of the grant
date, subject to continued employment. Payouts are made in shares and the value of an RSU award increases or decreases based on share price performance from the grant date, further aligning the interests of the executive with long-term shareholder
value creation. Before an RSU vests, the holder has no ownership rights in the shares and is not entitled to dividends or dividend equivalents. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>rTSR
PSUs </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">Twenty percent of each NEO&#8217;s fiscal year 2026 share-based long-term incentive award is in the form of rTSR PSUs. The rTSR
PSU awards granted in fiscal year 2026 will be earned (or not), at up to a maximum of 200% of target, based upon Flex&#8217;s percentile rank of TSR over a three-year period compared to the rTSR peer group companies (described below). Performance is
measured over three discrete measurement periods&#8212;of <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">12-,</FONT> <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">24-,</FONT> and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">36-months&#8212;within</FONT> each three-year cycle, as
illustrated below. The rTSR PSU final payout will be based on the average payouts of these three performance periods and does not occur until after the conclusion of the full <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">36-month</FONT> performance period. </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center">160 </P>

</DIV></Center>

 </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">The use of discrete measurement periods is intended to minimize the potential impact of short-term share
price volatility at the end of the performance period. In addition, having vesting occur following conclusion of the final three-year performance period aligns value delivery with longer-term absolute TSR performance. The Flex Compensation and
People Committee believes that this approach encourages NEOs to focus on generating long-term shareholder returns and results in payouts that more accurately reflect the shareholder experience over the full three-year cycle. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">The number of shares earned is dependent on the percentile rank achieved, within each of the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">12-,</FONT> <FONT

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">Flex has incorporated adjusted EPS growth PSUs into Flex&#8217;s LTI program since fiscal year 2022 to support continued focus on achieving
Flex&#8217;s long-term financial strategy. For FY26, these PSUs represent 47% of Flex&#8217;s participating NEOs&#8217; share-based long-term incentive awards (based on the target value of the awards as described below) and will be earned (or not),
at up to a maximum of 250% of target, based upon Flex&#8217;s achievement of adjusted EPS growth targets. Further, to the extent that Flex&#8217;s rTSR is in the bottom quartile of the peer group, as described above, EPS Growth PSU funding is capped
at 200% of target. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">In setting the adjusted EPS growth targets, the Flex Compensation and People Committee considered the following

 </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">Adjusted EPS growth rates will be calculated using <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</FONT>
adjustments summarized on page&nbsp;157 of this information statement. Adjusted EPS used for purposes of adjusted EPS growth PSU performance calculations will exclude the impact of extraordinary items or events that have an unanticipated impact,
corporate transactions (including acquisitions or dispositions), and other unusual or nonrecurring items. For purposes of adjusted EPS, the impact of unplanned share repurchases attributable to corporate transactions (including acquisitions or
dispositions) will also be excluded. The rationale for excluding the impact of significant items or events that have an unanticipated impact is to focus participants on factors within their control and preserve the incentive orientation of the plan
in the face of significant, unforeseen business disruptions or other events. The objective of excluding the impact of M&amp;A is to measure performance on the same basis and business composition as in place at the start of the performance period.
See also Annex A to this information statement for a reconciliation of GAAP to <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</FONT> financial measures. </P>

performance, as well as its stock price performance. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Other Long-Term Incentive Compensation Award Granted During FY26 </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">On June&nbsp;19, 2025, the Flex Board of Directors, upon the recommendation of the Flex Compensation and People Committee, approved the grant
of a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">one-time</FONT> supplemental equity award (the &#8220;Supplemental Equity Award&#8221;) to our CEO Revathi Advaithi. The grant is 100% performance-based with a target value of $25&nbsp;million and can only be
earned for the achievement of highly rigorous goals for the Flex&#8217;s data center business (which constitutes the business of Spinco) over a multi-year period, with funding subject to a payout cap tied to Flex&#8217;s rTSR for further
accountability to Flex&#8217;s shareholders. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify"><I>Rationale and Considerations for Granting the Supplemental Equity Award </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">The Flex Compensation and People Committee and the Flex Board of Directors determined that granting this
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">one-time</FONT> Supplemental Equity Award is in the best interests of the Flex and that the amount and terms of the award have been carefully tailored to fit Flex&#8217;s strategic objective of growing its data
center business, as well as Flex&#8217;s consistent long-term goal of incremental shareholder value creation. The Supplemental Equity Award was approved with the advice and input of the Flex Compensation and People Committee&#8217;s independent
compensation consultant, which included a review of relevant benchmarking data. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Award Size and Structure </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">The Supplemental Equity Award for Ms.&nbsp;Advaithi has a grant date fair value at target of $25&nbsp;million and consists entirely of <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">at-risk</FONT> PSUs, designed to lock in the CEO to drive execution of Flex&#8217;s Cloud and Power Infrastructure business growth strategy and unlock shareholder value. The Supplemental Equity Award vests based on
rigorous fiscal year 28 Cloud and Power Infrastructure business OP targets and includes a meaningful rTSR cap, as further described below. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">The Supplemental Equity Award cliff-vests after performance is certified following the end of the performance period, subject to
Ms.&nbsp;Advaithi&#8217;s continued service through such date. The number of PSUs earned, if any, will be primarily based on the performance of the Cloud and Power Infrastructure business measured at the end of fiscal year 2028, as noted above, with
payouts ranging from 0% to 250% of the target PSUs granted. The underlying performance goals are rigorous and, if achieved, are expected to drive significant shareholder value creation. </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">Since the grant date of the Supplemental Equity Award on June&nbsp;19, 2025, Flex has meaningfully outperformed relevant benchmarks with
respect to share price performance. Flex&#8217;s +221% TSR through June&nbsp;1, 2026 has delivered superior returns to Flex&#8217;s shareholders, compared to the S&amp;P 500 (+29%) and Flex&#8217;s compensation peer group (+92%) over the same
period. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt" ALIGN="center">

of incremental shareholder value creation, which has already borne fruit. Flex&#8217;s superior TSR performance since the grant date of the Supplemental Equity Award through June&nbsp;1, 2026 has resulted in $37.0&nbsp;billion in incremental value
creation for its shareholders. In addition, since Flex&#8217;s announcement on May&nbsp;5, 2026 of the planned <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off,</FONT> Flex shareholders have experienced $18.8&nbsp;billion in incremental value creation.

 </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">The Flex Board of Directors believes that Flex&#8217;s superior performance since the date of grant, as
well as the overwhelmingly positive market reaction to the announcement of the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off,</FONT> are clear indications that the Supplemental Equity Award is working as intended &#8211; focusing on the strategic
objective of growing the data center business, as well as creating incremental value for Flex&#8217;s shareholders. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">At the Distribution
Date, the Supplemental Equity Award will be converted into an award relating to Spinco stock with no changes to the original award terms, performance metrics and targets or the performance period described above or the termination provisions
described below. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Supplemental Equity Award Termination Provisions </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">To further enhance its retentive effect, the Supplemental Equity Award is subject to continued service requirements that are more restrictive
than those applicable to Flex&#8217;s standard equity awards. Unlike other outstanding equity awards held by Ms.&nbsp;Advaithi, if Ms.&nbsp;Advaithi retires, such retirement will not entitle her to accelerated or continued vesting of the
Supplemental Equity Award. Moreover, unlike other outstanding equity awards held by Ms.&nbsp;Advaithi, if Ms.&nbsp;Advaithi&#8217;s employment with Flex is terminated due to her Disability (as such term is defined in the plan), such termination will
not entitle her to accelerated or continued vesting of the Supplemental Equity Award. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">The agreement evidencing the Supplemental Equity
Award provides that if Ms.&nbsp;Advaithi&#8217;s employment with Flex is terminated (i)&nbsp;by Flex without &#8220;cause&#8221; or (ii)&nbsp;due to a voluntary termination for &#8220;good reason&#8221; (as each such term is defined in the award
agreement), in either case absent a change of control of Flex, Ms.&nbsp;Advaithi is entitled to ratable vesting of the Supplemental Equity Award determined by multiplying (x)&nbsp;the number of shares vesting based on actual performance measured at
the conclusion of the three-year performance period by (y)&nbsp;a fraction, the numerator of which is the number of days Ms.&nbsp;Advaithi provided services to Flex from the date of grant until her termination of employment, and the denominator of
which is the total number of days from the date of grant through the completion of the three-year performance period. The treatment of the Supplemental Equity Award in the event of Ms.&nbsp;Advaithi&#8217;s death will be the same as for other awards
of PSUs granted to Flex&#8217;s executive officers, as previously disclosed. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">Additionally, if Ms.&nbsp;Advaithi&#8217;s employment is
terminated (i)&nbsp;by Flex without &#8220;cause&#8221; or (ii)&nbsp;due to a voluntary termination for &#8220;good reason,&#8221; in either case during the period beginning on the consummation of a change of control of Flex and ending 24 months
following such change of control, Ms.&nbsp;Advaithi is entitled to 100% accelerated vesting of the Supplemental Equity Award based upon (x)&nbsp;actual performance if the three-year performance period is complete as of the date of such termination,
or (y)&nbsp;target performance if the three-year performance period is incomplete as of such termination. </P>

<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Payouts of Prior PSUs </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">The performance period for the rTSR PSUs granted in fiscal year 2023 ended in fiscal year 2026. The fiscal year 2023 rTSR PSU grants measured
Flex&#8217;s TSR relative to a custom peer group from June&nbsp;1, 2022 (the grant date), through June&nbsp;2, 2025 (the performance period end), using a trailing <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">20-day</FONT> average trading price for both the
beginning and the end of the performance period. Performance is measured over a three-year performance period with three discrete measurement periods&#8212;of <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">12-,</FONT> <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">24-,</FONT>
and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">36-</FONT> months&#8212;using an average of the three measurement periods to determine the final performance. The percentile ranking for the three measurement periods was an average of 88.83%, which was above the
75<SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">th</SUP> percentile, resulting in a 200% of target (maximum) payout for this award. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">The
performance period for the adjusted EPS growth-based PSUs granted in fiscal year 2024 ended in fiscal year 2026. Vesting was based on the Flex&#8217;s adjusted EPS growth, measured over a three-year period (April 1, 2023, through March&nbsp;31,
2026) in three discrete annual fiscal year measurements during the three-year performance period, and averaged with respect to all three adjusted EPS measurement periods. Flex&#8217;s fiscal year 2024 to 2026 adjusted EPS growth maximum goal was
12%. The actual adjusted EPS growth average was 18.9% over the three-year performance period, resulting in a maximum 200% of target payout for this award. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify"><B><I>Going Forward </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">Following the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off,</FONT> we intend for our long-term incentive award program to initially be similar to
Flex&#8217;s program. Our Compensation and People Committee will review our program with the goal of ensuring it is effective in attracting, retaining and motivating skilled executives and aligning the interests of management and shareholders. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Timing of Equity Award Grants </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify"><B><I>Flex
Practice </I></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">The Flex Compensation and People Committee approves all equity awards granted to its executive officers on or before the
grant date. Annual equity awards are typically granted to executive officers in June following the completion and release of financial results for the preceding fiscal year. The Flex Compensation and People Committee may also grant equity awards at
other times during the year due to special circumstances, including to new executive officers upon hire or promotion or a change in an executive officer&#8217;s role or scope of responsibilities. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">As a matter of good corporate governance, Flex does not grant equity awards in anticipation of the release of material nonpublic information
and, in any event, Flex does not time the release of material nonpublic information in coordination with grants of equity awards in a manner that intentionally benefits its executive officers. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify"><B><I>Going Forward </I></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">We
anticipate that our equity award grant practices initially will be comparable to those of Flex. Following the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off,</FONT> our Compensation and People Committee and management will review such practices to ensure
they meet our business and strategic needs and the objectives of our executive compensation program. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Benefits </B></P>

recommendations focused on personal and residential protection measures. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">During fiscal year 2026, Flex incurred limited personal security

<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify"><B><I>Going Forward </I></B></P>

Committee will review the benefits and perquisites provided by us to ensure they support our efforts to attract and retain talented executives. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Termination and Change of Control Arrangements </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">The Flex Board of Directors and the Flex Compensation and People Committee believe severance and change of control arrangements are important
components of the overall executive compensation program. Severance arrangements help attract and retain executives with the experience needed to drive success. Change of control provisions help to secure the continued employment and dedication of
the NEOs, to reduce any concern that they might have regarding their own continued employment prior to or following a change of control of Flex and to promote continuity of management during a corporate transaction. Accordingly, Flex maintains
certain arrangements, described below, pursuant to which the NEOs are entitled to certain severance and change of control protections. The benefits under these arrangements are described and quantified under the section titled &#8220;<I>Executive
Compensation&#8212;Potential Payments Upon Termination or Change of Control</I>.&#8221; Flex does not have employment agreements with any of our current NEOs. </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">We expect that we will adopt an executive severance plan substantially similar to the Flex Ltd. Executive Severance Plan. Following the

<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Executive Share Ownership Guidelines </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify"><B><I>Flex Practice </I></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">Flex
maintains robust share ownership guidelines in order to closely align the interests of senior management with those of Flex&#8217;s shareholders. The ownership guidelines for Flex&#8217;s executive officers are summarized below. </P>

<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Executive Incentive Compensation Recoupment Policy </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify"><B><I>Flex Practice </I></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">Flex
maintains an amended and restated Executive Incentive Compensation Recoupment Policy (the &#8220;Recoupment Policy&#8221;), as required by the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform&nbsp;&amp; Consumer Protection Act and corresponding listing standards
adopted by Nasdaq regarding compensation recovery. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">Flex&#8217;s Recoupment Policy applies in the event Flex is required to prepare an
accounting restatement due to material noncompliance with any financial reporting requirement under the federal securities laws, including any required accounting restatement to correct an error in previously issued financial statements that is
material to the previously issued financial statements, or that would result in a material misstatement if the error were corrected in the current period or left uncorrected in the current period (a &#8220;Financial Restatement&#8221;). Pursuant to
Flex&#8217;s Recoupment Policy, Flex will promptly recover any erroneously awarded incentive-based compensation, on a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">no-fault</FONT> basis, received by any current or former executive officer of Flex, including
Flex&#8217;s NEOs, during the three completed fiscal years immediately preceding the date on which Flex is required to prepare a Financial Restatement. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">In addition to erroneously awarded incentive-based compensation, under Flex&#8217;s Recoupment Policy, the Flex Compensation and People
Committee, as administrator of the Recoupment Policy, may, to the extent it deems appropriate, cancel outstanding equity awards, including time- or performance-based awards, where the Flex Board of Directors or the Flex Compensation and People
Committee took into account the financial performance of Flex in granting such awards and the financial results were subsequently reduced due to a Financial Restatement. The Recoupment Policy also provides that incentive compensation may be
recovered from certain other direct reports of Flex&#8217;s CEO under certain specified circumstances if deemed appropriate by the Flex Compensation and People Committee. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify"><B><I>Going Forward </I></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">Our
Compensation and People Committee is expected to adopt a substantially similar recoupment policy in connection with the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off.</FONT> </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Nonqualified Deferred Compensation in Fiscal Year 2026 </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">Each of the NEOs participates in Flex&#8217;s NQDC Plan. Flex&#8217;s deferred compensation program is intended to promote retention by
providing a long-term savings opportunity on a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">tax-efficient</FONT> basis. Under Flex&#8217;s NQDC Plan, participating officers may defer up to 70% of their base salary and bonus, net of certain statutory and benefit
deductions. Flex may make a discretionary matching contribution for these deferrals to reflect limitations on our matching contribution under the 401(k) plan. Under this plan, Flex may also make annual contributions, in amounts up to 37.5% of each
participant&#8217;s base salary (subject to offsets for <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-U.S.</FONT> executives&#8217; pension and other benefits), which will cliff-vest after four years. For these annual contributions, 50% of the funding is
paid as a percent of base salary and the remaining 50% is performance-based, up to a maximum of 150%. Amounts credited to the deferral accounts are deemed to be invested in hypothetical investments selected by a participant or an investment manager
on behalf of each participant. Participants in Flex&#8217;s NQDC Plan may receive their </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center">179 </P>

<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Potential Payments Upon Termination or Change of Control </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">As described in the section titled &#8220;<I>Compensation Discussion and Analysis</I>&#8221; of this information statement, our NEOs do not
have employment agreements with us. Our NEOs are eligible for certain termination and change of control benefits under the Flex Executive Severance Plan, Flex&#8217;s NQDC Plan and the Flex 2017 Equity Incentive Plan. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Acceleration of Vesting of Deferred Compensation </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">If the employment of any participant in Flex&#8217;s NQDC Plan is involuntarily terminated by Flex without cause or is terminated by the
executive with good reason within two years following a change of control (as defined in Flex&#8217;s NQDC Plan), the entire unvested portion of the deferred compensation account of the NEO will vest. The entire unvested portion of a
participant&#8217;s deferred compensation account also will vest if the NEO&#8217;s employment terminates as a result of death or disability. If a participant in Flex&#8217;s NQDC Plan ceases to provide services to Flex due to a qualifying
retirement (generally meaning a voluntary termination of service after the participant has attained the age of 55, completed at least 5 years of service as an employee of Flex, and the sum of age and service is equal to at least 65), the unvested
portion of the NEO&#8217;s deferred compensation account will continue to vest, subject to the NEO signing a release of claims, complying with post-termination restrictive covenants, and (if required by Flex in its discretion), providing up to 6
months advance written notice of retirement. As described below under the heading &#8220;<I>Executive Severance Plan</I>,&#8221; if the employment of a participant in Flex&#8217;s NQDC Plan is terminated by Flex without cause or by the NEO for good
reason, but not within two years following a change of control, the NEO generally would be entitled to continued vesting of the NEO&#8217;s deferred compensation account for a specified period following termination. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Acceleration of Vesting of Equity Awards </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">The number of unvested equity awards held by each NEO as of March&nbsp;31, 2026, is listed above in the Outstanding Equity Awards at 2026
Fiscal <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Year-End</FONT> table. All unvested outstanding equity awards held by the NEOs at the end of fiscal year 2026 were granted under the Flex 2017 Equity Incentive Plan. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">Subject to any waiver by the Flex Compensation and People Committee, all unvested RSU awards, PSU awards and unvested stock options held by a
plan participant will be forfeited if the participant ceases to provide services to Flex, except for certain termination reasons such as retirement, death, disability, or involuntary termination without cause or for &#8220;good reason&#8221; (as
defined in Flex&#8217;s Executive Severance Plan) within 24 months after a change of control. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Treatment of Certain Awards Upon Retirement </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">Certain award agreements for RSUs, rTSR PSUs, and adjusted EPS growth PSUs granted under the Flex 2017 Equity Incentive Plan provide that if a
plan participant ceases to provide services to Flex due to a qualifying retirement (meaning a voluntary termination of service after the participant has attained the age of fifty-five (55)&nbsp;years; completed at least five (5)&nbsp;years of
service as an employee of Flex; and the sum of age and service is equal to at least 65), then the award will not terminate. RSUs would continue to vest, and a pro rata number for the length of time employed during the performance period shall be
issued to the participant at the end of the performance cycle for rTSR PSUs and adjusted EPS growth PSUs. However, the Supplemental Equity&nbsp;Award PSUs granted to Ms.&nbsp;Advaithi during fiscal year 2026 and the PSUs and RSUs granted as
supplemental equity awards to Mr.&nbsp;Tan during fiscal year 2025, respectively, do not provide for accelerated or continued vesting upon retirement. Among our NEOs, Ms.&nbsp;Advaithi and Mr. Offer meet the retirement criteria. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Treatment of Certain Awards Upon Death or Disability </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">Certain award agreements for RSUs, rTSR PSUs, and adjusted EPS growth PSUs granted under the Flex 2017 Equity Incentive Plan provide that if a
plan participant ceases to provide services to Flex due to death or </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">The Flex 2017 Equity Incentive Plan is a &#8220;double trigger&#8221; equity plan, meaning that unvested equity awards vest immediately only if
(i)&nbsp;there is a change of control of Flex and (ii)(x) such awards are not converted, assumed or replaced by the successor or survivor corporation or (y)&nbsp;such awards are converted, assumed or replaced by the successor or survivor
corporation, and the participant incurs an involuntarily termination of service as described below. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">Under the terms of the Flex 2017
Equity Incentive Plan, unless otherwise provided in the applicable award agreement or other agreement between Flex and the participant, in the event of a change of control of Flex (as defined in the Flex 2017 Equity Incentive Plan) in which the
participant&#8217;s awards are not converted, assumed, or replaced by a successor or survivor corporation, or a parent or subsidiary thereof, then all forfeiture restrictions on such awards will lapse immediately prior to the change of control and,
following the consummation of such a change of control, all such awards will terminate and cease to be outstanding. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">Under the terms of
the Flex 2017 Equity Incentive Plan, as amended effective March&nbsp;5, 2025, with respect to both then-outstanding and future awards, where awards under the Flex 2017 Equity Incentive Plan are assumed or continued after a change of control, those
awards will be treated as follows in the event of a participant&#8217;s &#8220;Involuntary Termination of Service&#8221; within 24 months after the change of control: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

measurement period) has not been completed as of the participant&#8217;s Involuntary Termination of Service, or (ii)&nbsp;based upon the actual level of achievement of the applicable performance goals during the applicable performance period (or any

<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">For purposes of &#8220;double-trigger&#8221; vesting of equity awards in connection with a change of control, an &#8220;Involuntary
Termination of Service&#8221; means (a)&nbsp;the termination of the participant&#8217;s service by Flex (or any successor or survivor corporation, or a parent or subsidiary thereof) without &#8220;cause&#8221; (as defined in the Flex 2017 Equity
Incentive Plan) and not as a result of the participant&#8217;s death or disability, or (b)&nbsp;where the participant, such as each of the NEOs, is a party to an arrangement, such as the Flex Executive Severance Plan, that defines &#8220;good
reason&#8221; with respect to the participant, the participant&#8217;s termination of service for &#8220;good reason&#8221; as so defined. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Flex
Executive Severance Plan </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="justify">Flex&#8217;s Executive Severance Plan covers all of the NEOs and certain other senior level employees of
Flex. Under the Flex Executive Severance Plan, in the event of a qualifying termination of employment by the company </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center">182 </P>

</DIV></Center>
